title: Social Network
tagline: A Facebook-like platform with followers, groups, events and real-time chat. Go backend, Next.js frontend.
summary: A complete social platform built as a team: profiles, posts with privacy levels, groups with events, notifications and real-time chat. The backend is written in Go with SQLite and versioned migrations, and the frontend uses Next.js. Each side ships as its own Docker image.
problem: Build a social network from scratch without a backend framework: user accounts, a follow system that respects private profiles, posts that only the right people can see, groups with events, and a chat that updates in real time. The whole app had to run in two separate Docker containers.

features: Registration and login, with sessions kept in cookies and passwords hashed with bcrypt
Public and private profiles, with follow requests for private ones
Posts with three privacy levels: public, followers only, or selected followers
Groups with invitations, join requests, posts and events with RSVP
Private and group chat in real time over WebSockets (Gorilla)
Notifications for follow requests, group invitations, join requests and events
Image uploads in JPEG, PNG and GIF

challenges.title: Who is allowed to see this post?
challenges.problem: Every post has one of three privacy levels, and profiles can be public or private. One wrong check leaks private content.
challenges.solution: Visibility is checked by the Go backend on every request, from the post's privacy level and the follower relationships stored in SQLite. [TODO: confirm, and add how you wrote the check]

challenges.title: Chat and notifications in real time
challenges.problem: Messages and notifications must appear instantly, without reloading the page.
challenges.solution: Each logged-in user keeps a WebSocket connection open (Gorilla WebSocket), and the server pushes new messages and notifications to the right connections. [TODO: confirm how you tracked open connections]

challenges.title: Changing the database safely
challenges.problem: The schema changed many times while features were added by different teammates.
challenges.solution: Versioned SQL migration files managed with `golang-migrate`, so every teammate and every container builds exactly the same schema.

learned: Designing a relational schema for social features: followers, privacy levels, group membership
Session and cookie authentication without a framework
Splitting an app into two Docker images that work together
